work.title: Include the Work id in the GitHub Issue title
work.description: The Issue projection opens and reconciles Issues titled with the bare Work title, so an issue list or board shows prose with no stable handle — while refs, branches, and milestones all speak the INIT-x.y id. Prefix the Issue title with the Work id at creation, reconcile already-linked Issues to carry it on the next sync, and converge: a title that already carries the id is left alone. Matching keeps keying on the Work id, so a retitled Issue never maps to a duplicate.
acceptance: Publishing a Work opens its GitHub Issue with the Work id in the title
An Issue linked before this change is reconciled to carry the Work id in its title on the next sync
A repeated sync leaves an Issue untouched once its title carries the id, with no edit churn
Issue matching still maps the Issue to its Work, so no duplicate Issue is opened for a Work whose projected title changed

result.handoff:
# Plan: Include the Work id in the GitHub Issue title (INIT-2.2) ## Finding (P1) The Issue title is managed in exactly two places: 1. Creation — publication.ts:207: `this.github.create(..., { title: entry.work.title, ... })`. 2. Reconcile — publication/reconcile.ts:60: `issue.title === entry.work.title ? {} : { title: entry.work.title }`. Issue matching (publication/mapping.ts) associates an Issue with a Work through three signals — the hidden body marker, the stored issue link, and requestedBy — and never reads the title. Retitling therefore cannot create a duplicate mapping; acceptance 4 is structurally safe and a test pins it. scripts/projection-e2e.mjs locates Issues by body and documentation.test.ts requires no title assertion, so the E2E scenario needs no change. ## Product files Build touches 1. src/core/identifiers.ts — add `WORK_CODE = /^INIT-\d+\.\d+$/` and `workCodeOf(workId: string): string` (extracts `INIT-.

` from a slugged Work id; INIT-2.4 will reuse both). 2. src/application/publication/reconcile.ts — add and export `desiredIssueTitle(work: WorkIdentity): string` beside desiredIssueBody, returning `${workCodeOf(work.id)}: ${work.title}`; use it in reconcileIssueContent in place of `entry.work.title` (both the comparison and the update). 3. src/application/publication.ts — the create call uses `desiredIssueTitle(entry.work)` instead of `entry.work.title`. 4. src/test/publication.test.ts — new and extended tests. Nothing else changes: matching, markers, milestones, the body section, and requestedBy handling are untouched. The body marker keeps the full slugged id. ## Rules - Format: `INIT-2.2: Include the Work id in the GitHub Issue title` — the short INIT-x.y code, a colon, a space, then the Work title. Not the full slugged id (unreadable) and not a bracketed suffix (the id belongs at the front, where lists sort and scan). - Creation and reconcile share the one helper, so the title an Issue opens with and the title drift reconciles to can never diverge. - Convergence is the existing mechanism: reconcileIssueContent compares and only edits on difference, so once the title carries the code a repeated sync makes no edit. - A human-edited title is reconciled back to the managed form, exactly as today — the Issue is a projection, not a second place to author the Work. ## Tests (src/test/publication.test.ts) 1. Extend the issue-creation test: the created Issue's title is `INIT-0.1: ` (acceptance 1). 2. Reconcile a pre-existing linked Issue: an Issue whose title is the bare Work title (the pre-change form, e.g. via the requestedBy or link path) gains the prefixed title on the next sync (acceptance 2). 3. Convergence: after a sync that set the prefixed title, a repeated sync reports the Issue unchanged and issues no edit (acceptance 3). 4. Duplicate safety: after retitling, matching still maps the Issue to its Work — a scoped publication detects the link, no new Issue is created, and the mapping conflict guards stay silent (acceptance 4). 5. workCodeOf is covered through these behavior-level assertions; no new core test file. ## Acceptance coverage 1. Opens with the id in the title — desiredIssueTitle at creation + test 1. 2. Pre-change linked Issues reconciled — desiredIssueTitle at reconcile + test 2. 3. No edit churn — existing compare-then-edit + test 3. 4. Matching unaffected — mapping never reads titles (structural) + test 4. ## Verification for Build npm run verify (typecheck, unit tests, smoke, --help). ## Non-goals No change to the E2E scenario, the body marker (keeps the full id), milestone sections, or Issue matching. No dependency on INIT-2.4, though identifiers.ts gains the WORK_CODE regex it will reuse.
